chapter: Singers, Las Vegas, Hodges and road life
title: Eddie Bert and Trummy Young evading marshals
summary: Trummy Young was hidden in the flies and then in Chubby Jackson's bass case to escape police over his wife's desertion complaint, but federal marshals met them in Boston.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Bert, B-e-r-t. Well, he was in the band at the same time that Trummy Young was. And of course they had quite a contest, because Eddie Bert was a very aggressive soloist, and as you know, so was Trummy. And it was a lot of fun, spelling them off against each other.
I've got to tell you a story about Trummy Young.

We were playing the Howard Theater in Washington, and it seems that Trummy's wife was after him. And I came off the stage -- while an act was on, and here's all of these policemen there. The guy said, "We're after Trummy Young." I said, "What for?" He said, "Well, his wife, desertion and all this." So the next number on the bill happened to be "Mood Indigo," which starts off with a trio

up at the microphone of Trummy Young and a trumpet player and a clarinet. So that's the way it started off. Now the stage is very dark and now the trumpet -- the spotlight goes back to the trumpet section for an open trumpet solo by, I think at that time -- I think it was probably -- that was still Peanuts. And I got the word to Trummy. I said, "These guys are here waiting." So he got the stagehand, and we hoisted Trummy up in the flies, on a rope, up in the flies there. Now, it comes back to the trio at the end of the thing, now here is Eddie Bert, and the clarinet, you know, up there playing the thing. Now, these guys were furious. They said, "What are you pulling?" I said, "I didn't pull anything. We've got over 2,500 people out there in the audience. What do you mean pull anything?" "Well, you did something." I said, "I didn't do a thing. You can't prove a thing. How could I do anything? I'm not a magician, I'm a musician." Well, now we've got Chubby Jackson's -- that was our closing day there, and we were going to Boston, the RKO Theater in Boston. So we got Chubby Jackson's bass case and we put Trummy in it, and he was taken down to the station in the bass case on the truck, you know, and they couldn't find him. Oh, they were furious. Now, we forgot one thing. The story should have had a nice ending, everybody got away, but these were United States Marshal/s, being the District of Columbia. So when we arrived

in Boston they had another set of them waiting there for us because it was a federal charge. And it took my attorney all he could do to keep me and Trummy out of jail, and I had to come up with some money for Trummy's wife and everything. But we got a big kick out of that, you can see.
And Chubby got his bass out too, right?
Well, he said, 'I want my bass with me,' you know.
Life on the road was just one big adventure.
